who: Hugh D. Hudson Jr., historian of Russia at Georgia State University, PhD University of North Carolina.

evidence.says: The authority cites The Rise of the Demidov Family and the Russian Iron Industry (1986), naming Hugh D. Hudson Jr. at Georgia State University.
Georgia State's 1996 catalog lists Hugh D. Hudson Jr., professor of history, with a PhD from the University of North Carolina.
The 2009–2010 graduate catalog names Hugh Hudson as chair of Georgia State's history department.

notes: The LC record explicitly supplies the student's institution; the university catalog also agrees with own_phd on the doctoral institution. The 1981 doctoral year was not independently checked.

who: Robert Louis Jenkins, historian at Mississippi State University, PhD Mississippi State 1978.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Robert L. Jenkins as Robert Louis Jenkins, author of The Gadsden Treaty and Sectionalism (1978).
Printed page 284 lists Robert L. Jenkins as associate professor of history, with Mississippi State degrees including a 1978 PhD.
The biographical entry expands the name to Robert Louis Jenkins, gives a 1978 Mississippi State PhD in United States history, and places his history faculty career there from 1979.
Mississippi State's history department identifies Robert L. Jenkins as associate professor emeritus.

notes: Full name, institution, field, doctoral year and faculty period agree. The separate candidate n2001055166, attached to The Malcolm X Encyclopedia, may be another record for this historian; that possible duplication is not resolved here.

who: Enno E. Kraehe, historian of Metternich and European diplomacy, Kentucky faculty 1948–1964, PhD Minnesota 1948.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Enno E. Kraehe through Metternich's German Policy (1963–1983).
Robert D. Billinger Jr.'s Central European History memorial gives Kraehe's Minnesota PhD in 1948, Kentucky teaching in 1948–1964, and authorship of the two volumes of Metternich's German Policy.

notes: The doctoral institution and year match exactly. The memorial places his departure from Kentucky in 1964, before the listed 1967–1971 dissertation completions; continued supervision after departure was not independently established.

who: George M. Kren, Kansas State historian of the Holocaust and psychohistory, with a University of Wisconsin doctorate.

who: David R. Maciel, University of New Mexico historian of Chicano and Latin American history, PhD UC Santa Barbara.
